finding_statement: Within SRC010's source-defined reference periods, the reported < Rp100,000/day category is 11.6% before the pandemic, 66.0% during the pandemic, and 40.4% in the 2022 fieldwork period; the > Rp100,000–Rp250,000 category is 54.4%, 26.2%, and 52.5% respectively.
caveat: Pre-pandemic and pandemic values are retrospective recall within the 2022 survey, not independent panel/survey waves; the income layer is not identified as gross, receipt, or net.

finding_statement: SRC029 reports its mixed fuel + food/drink bundle at 31.0% of gross daily earnings, while SRC013 reports 46.0%.
caveat: The bundle includes personal food/drink expenditure and is not project operating cost; sources differ in period, geography, and sampling context.

finding_statement: The share reporting seven workdays per week is 49.3% in SRC030, 42.2% in SRC029, and 55.5% in SRC013.
caveat: Different periods, geographies, and survey contexts prevent treating these points as a directly comparable national trend.

finding_statement: A 20% application-deduction category is reported by 52.9% of SRC029 respondents and 50.3% of SRC013 respondents.
caveat: These are driver-reported category prevalences, not transaction-level realized deduction rates and not automatic evidence of platform commission.

finding_statement: For aligned SRC029 source means (n=186; 2022–2023; Jabodetabek), gross service earnings equal Rp15,272.73 per source-reported working hour and Rp16,800 per completed order.
caveat: Both values are ratios of source means, not mean individual-driver ratios; the working-hour basis remains source_reported_unspecified and the values are gross, not net.

finding_statement: Project net operating earnings remain not computable from the current committed evidence because the complete same-observation gross-to-net chain is missing driver receipts before operating cost, driver-side platform deduction, and fuel cost.
caveat: Source-defined net income is not substituted for project net operating earnings, and missing components are not imputed.

finding_statement: Within SRC013, 51.0% report 9–12 source-reported working hours per day, 55.5% report seven workdays per week, and 52.8% report completing 6–10 orders per day.
caveat: These are separate source-specific prevalence measures and must not be added together or generalized to all Indonesian ojol drivers; SRC013 locality count remains internally inconsistent at 62 versus 67 kabupaten/kota.
